worked_example.problem: Triangle A′B′C′ is the image of ABC by a reflection. AB = {l} cm and Â = {a}°. Find A′B′ and Â′.
steps: A reflection keeps lengths: A′B′ = AB = {l} cm.

cards.idea: Symmetry keeps parallel and perpendicular lines, and points on a line.

right.text: The image of two perpendicular lines by a reflection is two perpendicular lines.
The image of three points on a line by a half turn is three points on a line.
The image of two parallel lines by a reflection is two parallel lines.

wrong.text: The image of a square by a reflection can be a rectangle that is not a square.
wrong.explain: Symmetry keeps lengths, so all four sides stay equal.

wrong.text: The image of an angle of 30° by a half turn is an angle of 150°.
wrong.explain: Symmetry keeps angles: it is still 30°.

wrong.text: The image of a segment of 4 cm by a reflection is a segment of 8 cm.

questions.prompt: [A′B′] is the image of [AB] by point symmetry. AB = {l} cm. Find A′B′.

misconceptions.explain: The image is the same size: point symmetry does not stretch.

questions.prompt: Triangle A′B′C′ is the image of ABC by a reflection. B̂ = {a}°. Find B̂′.

misconceptions.explain: A reflection keeps angles: the image angle is equal.
